To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lensing magnification affects the number counts of SMGs and that this effect is important in interpreting SZ observations of clusters.

(i) magnification by foreground haloes affects the number counts of submillimeter sources and (ii) this effect can be significant for high-redshift sources and for sources that are intrinsically more numerous than the observed counts.

magnification of high-z galaxies by intervening groups and clusters is significant, affecting the counts of high-z sources by about 60% and the SZ signal of massive clusters by a factor of 2, while the SZ signal of low-mass, low-redshift clusters is dominated by the Poisson noise of high-z galaxies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important aspects of cosmological observations: the number counts of galaxies at high redshifts and the contamination of SZ observations by the high-redshift galaxy populations.
the effects of lensing by intervening galaxy groups/clusters on high-redshift source populations and the SZ signal of clusters.

two aspects of lensing: (i) the effect of lensing magnification on the observed counts of high-red-shift galaxies, and (ii) the effect of the high-redshift galaxy background on the SZ signal of clusters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effect of magnification on counts of SMGs is significant and needs to be accounted for in future surveys, whereas the SZ signal of clusters can be significantly contaminated by the Poisson noise of SMGs, which needs to be modelled carefully in future SZ surveys.
magnification effects need to be carefully considered in any high-redshift galaxy or SZ cluster survey.
magnification effects should be included in the analysis of SZ surveys, and that the effects are significant for a large number of clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lensing magnification is important for the interpretation of high-redshift source counts, especially for SMGs and SZ surveys.
the lensing magnification effects are important for high-redshift source counts and for SZ observations, especially if the intrinsic source counts are steeper than observed.
the lensing effects are important for both the number counts of SMGs and the SZ observations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lensing magnification can have a large effect on the observed number counts of high- z galaxies and on the contamination from these galaxies on SZ observations of clusters.
the effects of lensing on high-redshift galaxy counts are significant, especially for the steep part of the counts.
magnification effects are very important for both high-redshift galaxy counts and SZ observations, and need to be taken into account in the analysis.
